name: Agda
note: dependent types as a programming language
typeSystem: Full dependent types based on intuitionistic type theory (in the Martin-Lof tradition), with inductive families, a totality checker, and support for both writing programs and mechanising mathematical proofs via the Curry-Howard correspondence.
runtime: Agda programs are elaborated and type-checked interactively (commonly in Emacs), then compiled via a backend; interactive normalization is also available for exploring checked definitions.

runtimes.name: MAlonzo (GHC backend)
runtimes.role: Default backend: compiles Agda to Haskell, then to a native binary via GHC.

runtimes.name: JavaScript backend
runtimes.role: Compiles Agda to JavaScript for running in a browser or Node.js.

compilers.name: agda
compilers.role: The reference type checker and compiler, itself written in Haskell.

concurrencyModel: Agda's core language has no concurrency primitives. Backend-specific concurrency can be reached through foreign-function interfaces or bindings, so its availability and semantics depend on the selected backend.

codeExample.caption: A length-indexed vector and a totality-checked append
codeExample.source:
module VecAppend where

open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_)

data Vec (A : Set) : Nat -> Set where
  []  : Vec A zero
  _::_ : {n : Nat} -> A -> Vec A n -> Vec A (suc n)

append : {A : Set} {n m : Nat} -> Vec A n -> Vec A m -> Vec A (n + m)
append [] ys = ys
append (x :: xs) ys = x :: append xs ys
